phase3_findings.description: New schedulewakeup-disable-cron-probe arm sets CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_CRON at JOB env, not step env; claude-code-action's step-level env can shadow a job-env var (per CLAUDE.md's Bedrock note), so the variable-under-test may never reach the CLI subprocess. The measurement could silently become inert while still producing a plausible-looking execution file — an operator would read 'measured X' when the var was never in effect. Sibling background-tasks-probe sets its var-under-test at step level. Repo-internal probe only; no shipped behavior depends on it.

Docstring (~line 385) and inline comment (lines 428-429) claim 'an unrecognized denial shape yields no name and fails safe (no ship), never a false one', but the else branch for a non-dict permission_denials entry does denial_names.append(str(d)) — not 'no name'. A bare-string entry whose str contains the token would set sw_denied and gate a SHIP (the serialized-substring vector the change claims to close). The guarantee is accurate only for the dict-with-no-recognized-keys case; it overgeneralizes to all unrecognized shapes.
phase3_findings.cap_rationale: Code-comment/docstring in a repo-internal probe helper. Limb one holds: no tool parses the comment to decide behavior. Limb two holds: not a user-facing/published surface read by anyone outside the repo (matcher-probe.yml and this helper are repo-internal, not shipped by install.sh). Both inertness limbs hold, so the behavior-inert prose cap covers it -> capped to Suggestion, outside the self-contradicting-diff carve-out, drives no REJECT at the critical threshold.

phase3_findings.description: The multi-key denial-name lookup denial_names.append(' '.join(str(d.get(k,'')) for k in ('tool','tool_name','name'))) is exercised only through the 'tool' key; no fixture records a denial as {'tool_name':'ScheduleWakeup'} or {'name':'ScheduleWakeup'}. A regression dropping tool_name/name from the tuple would leave every assertion green while silently reverting a SHIP verdict to INCONCLUSIVE on a harness spelling the field either way. Newly-reachable SHIP-gating path with no covering assertion.

The non-dict denial else: str(d) branch has no covering fixture; a regression replacing it with '' (dropping the shape) would go undetected. Lower criticality: the dict shape is the realistic harness output and dropping it fails safe (no ship).
